title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Public Health Officer (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Public Health Officer (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: A 68 year old man is admitted to hospital with a complaint of intermittent lower abdominal pain, bowel habit changes and rectal bleeding one month duration. He has tenesmus and incomplete sensation of defecation and has lost weight. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms and age suggest colorectal cancer as the most likely diagnosis.

questions.questionText: Of the strategies to reduce maternal mortality, which one of the following interventions is most effective in reducing the likelihood of developing pregnancy related complications?
questions.explanation: Family planning is the most effective strategy to reduce maternal mortality by preventing unintended pregnancies and allowing for appropriate birth spacing, directly reducing the number of women exposed to pregnancy-related complications.

questions.questionText: Which of the following samples gives the highest yield for diagnosing visceral Leishmaniasis?
questions.explanation: Splenic aspirate has the highest sensitivity (95-98%) for diagnosing visceral leishmaniasis compared to bone marrow (60-85%), lymph node aspirate (60%), or blood samples. It allows direct visualization of the Leishmania parasite, though carries a slightly higher risk of complications.

questions.questionText: Which of the following micro-nutrients enhances the absorption of iron?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C enhances the absorption of iron.

questions.questionText: A 25 year-old male with known liver disease presents with cough, fever and weight loss for one month. Sputum examination for acid fast bacilli is positive 3 times. Which combination anti-tuberculosis treatment is most appropriate for this patient?
questions.explanation: For patients with liver disease and tuberculosis, the regimen 2ERHZ/4HE (Ethambutol, Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide for 2 months followed by Isoniazid and Ethambutol for 4 months) is appropriate as it reduces hepatotoxicity risk while providing effective treatment.

questions.questionText: A 55 year-old man presented to the surgical OPD with rectal bleeding of one month duration. He has no protruding mass per rectum and digital rectal examination was non-revealing. What is the next best step in managing this patient?
questions.explanation: Colonoscopy is the gold standard diagnostic tool for evaluating rectal bleeding, allowing direct visualization of the entire colon and rectum while providing the opportunity to biopsy suspicious lesions or remove polyps if identified.

questions.questionText: A 35 year-old woman presented with four episodes of spasm, generalized rigidity and trismus after she sustained a puncture over the left foot two days ago. She is fully conscious. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
questions.explanation: Diazepam is appropriate for managing muscle spasms and rigidity.

questions.questionText: A 17 year-old student came to a clinic seeking pregnancy termination service at gestational age of 10 weeks. She gave a history of sexual assault. Which of the following is the best method of termination of pregnancy for this case?
questions.explanation: Manual vacuum aspiration is a safe and effective method for early pregnancy termination.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct percentage of dextrose to treat neonatal hypoglycemia?
questions.explanation: 10% dextrose is the standard treatment for neonatal hypoglycemia.

questions.questionText: In health center hazardous waste disposal was found to be a critical problem. Which of the following waste disposal options is the most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Incinerating is the most appropriate method for hazardous waste disposal.

questions.questionText: The data collected about a body mass index of physically active population looks positively skewed. Which measures of central tendency is advisable to be used for such types of data?
questions.explanation: For positively skewed data, the median is the most appropriate measure of central tendency as it is not influenced by extreme values. The mean would be pulled toward the higher values, while variance and range are measures of dispersion, not central tendency.

questions.questionText: A 30 year-old man collapses at a wedding and is witnessed to have seizure lasting two minutes. When a paramedic arrives and calls his name and asks some questions he mumbles and no one could hear what he said. When pressure was applied to his nail bed he opened his eyes, rubbed his nail and pushed away the hand holding his nail bed. What is his Glasgow coma scale (GCS)?
questions.explanation: The GCS is calculated based on eye opening (3 points - opens eyes to painful stimulus), verbal response (3 points - inappropriate words/mumbling), and motor response (5 points - localizes pain by pushing away hand), totaling 11 points.

questions.questionText: If your aim is to bring behavioral change in hygiene and sanitation among a rural population, the best theory/model you can use for planning the change will be:
questions.explanation: The PRECEDE-PROCEED model is particularly effective for community-level health promotion interventions like hygiene and sanitation behavior change. It provides a comprehensive framework that addresses social, epidemiological, behavioral, educational, administrative, and evaluation factors, making it more suitable than individual-focused models like Health Belief Model or Trans-theoretical Model.

questions.questionText: A health officer is evaluating a patient with lymphoma. Which of the following lymph node characteristics are least likely?
questions.explanation: Matted lymph nodes with discharging sinus are characteristic of tuberculosis lymphadenitis or other suppurative infections, not lymphoma. Lymphoma typically presents with firm, rubbery, discrete, mobile, and non-tender lymph nodes without discharge or matting.

questions.questionText: A 34 year-old primigravida lady comes with cessation of fetal movement of four days duration at gestational age of 35 weeks. She is otherwise asymptomatic and has no medical problems. Examination shows stable vital signs, symphysiofundal height of 34cms, no uterine contraction and absent fetal heart beat. What is the best initial step in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is the best initial step to confirm fetal status.

questions.questionText: A zonal health Department head assigned a budget for different tasks for a fiscal year. Which decisional role did he play?
questions.explanation: Resource allocation is a key role in budget management.

questions.questionText: The number of modes of transmission has an effect on the control or eradication of infectious disease. From this perspective, which of the following diseases is more difficult to control?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary tuberculosis is more difficult to control due to its airborne transmission.

questions.questionText: A 30 year-old man presented to the emergency surgical OPD with perianal pain and bright red rectal bleeding during defecation. He has fever chills. Perianal examination showed shallow laceration posteriorly. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The presence of fever and chills suggests infection, which combined with perianal pain and posterior laceration indicates a perirectal abscess. Simple anal fissures do not typically cause fever, while fistulas are chronic conditions and thrombosed hemorrhoids present with a painful lump without fever.

questions.questionText: A significant number of under-five children were diagnosed with serious neurological problems and anemia in a certain district. Researchers found out that the families of these children were strict vegetarians. Which nutritional deficiency are the children suffering from?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency is common in strict vegetarians since it's primarily found in animal products. In children, B12 deficiency can cause megaloblastic anemia and serious neurological problems including developmental delay, irritability, weakness, and failure to thrive. Neither folate nor B3/B6 deficiencies typically present with this combination of neurological and hematological findings.

questions.questionText: A 52 year-old female presents to the clinic with four months of fatigue, lower extremity burning pain and numbness. Laboratory test reveals Hgb=8.5g/dl, MCV=118fl, WBC=4000/μl and platelets=150,000/μl. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The high MCV and symptoms suggest vitamin B12 deficiency anemia.

questions.questionText: A 64 year-old male patient presented to the Emergency OPD after he failed to pass urine for 24 hours. He had difficulty of urination for the last one year. The previous night he took seven bottles of beer with friends. On examination he is acutely sick looking in pain. Bladder is palpable 10 cm above the pubic bone and tender. What is the most likely cause for this acute urinary retention?
questions.explanation: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is the most likely cause of acute urinary retention in this elderly male with chronic urinary symptoms. Alcohol consumption worsened the condition by causing increased urinary production, prostatic congestion, and decreased awareness of bladder fullness - all precipitating factors for acute retention in a patient with underlying BPH.

questions.questionText: A 30 year-old prisoner presents with intermittent fever and headache of two days duration. He claims that five of his roommates had similar symptoms and were treated in the prison. Blood film examination showed a spirochete. Which one of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic choice for that patient?
questions.explanation: The clinical scenario suggests louse-borne relapsing fever (Borrelia recurrentis), especially in crowded settings like prisons. Procaine penicillin is the drug of choice for treating spirochetal infections including relapsing fever. Ceftriaxone is an alternative but often reserved for more severe cases, while ciprofloxacin and vancomycin are not effective against spirochetes.

questions.questionText: A researcher who conducted a study on malnutrition among under-five children found out a high prevalence of stunting in that community. What does this finding imply?
options: High rate of genetic growth defect
questions.explanation: Stunting (low height for age) indicates chronic malnutrition and reflects long-standing nutritional problems in a community. Stunting develops over a long period due to inadequate nutrition and repeated infections, particularly during the first 1000 days of life. Unlike wasting (low weight for height) which indicates acute malnutrition, stunting is a marker of persistent socioeconomic challenges affecting nutrition over extended periods. Stunting has long-term consequences including impaired cognitive development, reduced school performance, and decreased economic productivity in adulthood.

questions.questionText: A para III mother who gave birth to an alive male neonate at home before an hour was brought to a hospital because of restlessness and protrusion of mass per vaginum. She is acutely sick looking, BP is not recordable, PR=132/min, and feeble RR=20/min. T=36°c. A globular fleshy mass with minimal bleeding protruding through the introitus. What is the most appropriate initial step in management of this patient?
questions.explanation: Resuscitation with IV fluids is critical in this acutely sick patient.

questions.questionText: A 36 year old woman came with complaints of malaise, chills and fever. She also had nausea, headache and anorexia. She reported occasional IV drug use. On auscultation, a loud holosystolic murmur is detected. What is the next best step to confirm the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation suggests infective endocarditis, common in IV drug users. Echocardiography is the best non-invasive test to visualize valve vegetations, valvular damage, and cardiac function. Blood cultures should also be obtained, but among the options given, echocardiogram is most appropriate.

questions.questionText: A 6 week old infant presented with high grade fever three hours after he took the first of his scheduled vaccines. On examination he is febrile and irritable; otherwise there are no findings in other systems. What is the most appropriate management for this infant?
questions.explanation: Admitting and observing the infant is appropriate due to the fever after vaccination.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a component of prerequisites for forceps application?
questions.explanation: Vertex presentation is essential for the safe application of forceps.

questions.questionText: A 9 month old boy is brought to a health center in an unresponsive state after repeated episodes of vomiting and diarrhea. Physical examination showed a rapid and feeble pulse, skin pinch returns very slowly. Multiple attempts to secure an IV line have failed. What is the next best step in the management of this infant?
options: Do blood film and determine blood glucose
Give ORS through NG-tube and refer
Obtain blood sample for complete blood count
questions.explanation: In severe dehydration with failed IV access attempts, nasogastric rehydration with ORS is a life-saving intervention and the most appropriate next step. This allows for fluid replacement while arrangements are made for referral to a higher facility for potential intraosseous access or more intensive management.

questions.questionText: A 51 year-old man came to your OPD complaining he can't read contact numbers from his mobile phone since 6 months. He used to be able to read by holding the phone further away. He has no other ocular complaints. He had 6/6 distance vision on both eyes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Presbyopia is the age-related loss of near vision.

questions.questionText: A health extension worker divided participants of a certain kebele into different groups to discuss the district's main health problems and provided feedback on the main findings to the whole group. What type of method is implemented?
questions.explanation: Buzz group discussions are effective for engaging participants in health problem discussions.

questions.questionText: A 62 year-old woman with heart failure develops pneumonia and large pleural effusion. Laboratory investigation shows serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 420mg/dl and serum protein 8g/dl. Thoracentesis is performed in an effort to determine if the pleural effusion is due to HF or pneumonia. Which of the following findings would indicate that the pleural effusion is due to HF?
questions.explanation: A low pleural fluid LDH (100mg/dl) suggests a transudate, which is typical of heart failure. Heart failure pleural effusions are characterized by low protein and LDH levels, while exudative effusions (as in pneumonia) have high protein and LDH, low glucose, and low pH.

questions.questionText: A young man consumed 100 gram serving of whole wheat spaghetti containing 10 grams of protein, 40 grams of carbohydrate and 5 grams of fat. What is the estimated content in kcal?
questions.explanation: To calculate the caloric content: Protein (4 kcal/g × 10g = 40 kcal) + Carbohydrates (4 kcal/g × 40g = 160 kcal) + Fat (9 kcal/g × 5g = 45 kcal) = 245 kcal total.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is recommended for treating Chlamydia trachomatis infection?
questions.explanation: Doxycycline (100mg twice daily for 7 days) is a first-line treatment for Chlamydia trachomatis infections. Azithromycin is an alternative. Metronidazole is used for anaerobic infections, fluconazole for fungal infections, and gentamicin for gram-negative bacterial infections.

questions.questionText: Which of the following isn't a component of active 3rd stage management?
questions.explanation: Nipple stimulation is not a standard component of active management of the 3rd stage of labor.

questions.questionText: A 2 year-old child presented with difficulty of breathing of two hours. He had a barking cough and hoarseness of voice for the last two days. On physical exam he is agitated, has audible stridor at rest and lower chest indrawing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Croup syndrome is characterized by barking cough and stridor.

questions.questionText: A 5 year old child is diagnosed with Group A beta-hemolytic tonsillo-pharyngitis. Which one is a non-suppurative complication of this condition?
questions.explanation: Rheumatic fever is a non-suppurative complication of Group A strep infection.

questions.questionText: Which one is the main reason for low contraceptive use in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: According to demographic and health surveys in Ethiopia, fear of side effects and health concerns are the most commonly cited reasons for not using contraceptives. Religious beliefs, partner opposition, and use of breastfeeding as a natural method are also factors, but fear of side effects is most prevalent.

questions.questionText: A 22 years old HIV positive man with a presumptive diagnosis of pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia has no signs of respiratory distress. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
questions.explanation: Cotrimoxazole is the first-line treatment for pneumocystis pneumonia.

questions.questionText: A 21 year-old GII PI mother at 24 weeks gestation complains of severe vulvar itching and cotton cheese-like discharge. A wet mount slide shows no clue cells but hyphae. Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The presence of hyphae indicates a Candida infection.

questions.questionText: A 29 year-old woman presents with vaginal pruritus associated with white curd-like discharge. On examination, there is an erythematous macular lesion but no vesicles. Investigation shows no clue cells, negative whiff test. Which of the following is the treatment of choice for this case?
questions.explanation: Fluconazole is the treatment of choice for Candida infections.

questions.questionText: Which of the following contraceptive methods is the most effective?
questions.explanation: The intrauterine contraceptive device is one of the most effective contraceptive methods.

questions.questionText: In the active management of the 3rd stage of labor, if the placenta failed to be delivered by controlled cord traction, which one is the next best management?
questions.explanation: Manual removal of the placenta is necessary if it does not deliver spontaneously.

questions.questionText: Some experts argue that WHO's definition for maternal mortality has limitations. What is its limitation in measuring maternal mortality ratio?
options: It disregards deaths that occur after 42 days
It misses major causes of maternal death
It misses the time most maternal deaths occur
questions.explanation: The WHO definition of maternal mortality only includes deaths during pregnancy or within 42 days after termination of pregnancy. This excludes late maternal deaths (occurring between 43 days and one year postpartum) that may still be related to pregnancy complications or their management, leading to underestimation of pregnancy-related mortality.

questions.questionText: A 26 year-old GIII PI woman at 20 weeks of gestation came for antenatal care follow-up. Previous obstetric history was unremarkable. Which of the following cardiac findings requires further evaluation?
questions.explanation: A diastolic murmur at any stage of pregnancy is abnormal and requires further evaluation as it suggests valvular pathology, whereas a grade II systolic murmur, third heart sound, and moderate shifting of PMI can be normal findings in pregnancy due to increased blood volume.

questions.questionText: A 3 month old infant has rhinorrhea, cough and noisy breath. Physical examination reveals RR=72/min, PR=142/min and T=37.8°c. He is irritable and has diffuse wheezes and chest retraction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Bronchiolitis is characterized by wheezing and respiratory distress in infants.

questions.questionText: A 53 year-old man comes to the Hospital complaining of poor appetite, loss of pleasure in daily activities, sleeplessness, and decreased libido for 3 weeks. He is contemplating retiring, expressing concern that his poor performance in his job. On mental status examination he shows empty feeling and makes two errors in subtraction serial 3's from 20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are consistent with major depressive disorder.

questions.questionText: A 60 year old man had cirrhosis of the liver secondary to hepatitis B for years. In the last couple of months his jaundice started to worsen and developed sleep disturbance. He also complained of vague, right upper quadrant pain since four weeks. Physical examination shows a rough, nodular liver. Which one is an additional useful diagnostic test for this patient?
questions.explanation: Alpha-fetoprotein is a tumor marker that can indicate hepatocellular carcinoma.

questions.questionText: If a health officer wants to know the risk of maternal death due to level of fertility and risk of maternal death per pregnancy or per birth, which measure of maternal mortality should he/she use?
options: Life time risk of maternal mortality
questions.explanation: The maternal mortality rate measures the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 women of reproductive age, reflecting both the risk of death per pregnancy and the fertility rate in a population. The maternal mortality ratio (option A) measures the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births and only reflects the risk of death once a woman is pregnant.

questions.questionText: A 3 year old boy came to the OPD with diarrhea. Stool examination revealed trophozoite of Giardia lamblia. What is the first line drug to treat this parasite?
questions.explanation: Metronidazole is the first-line treatment for Giardia lamblia.

questions.questionText: A mother brought a 20 day-old male neonate that failed to move his right extremity since five days of age after delivery at home. On examination, the right distal thigh is grossly swollen. The skin is shiny and tender. Laboratory work up showed elevated WBC count with a left shift, ESR was elevated. X-ray showed periosteal reaction with distortion of the soft tissue fat plane. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Acute osteomyelitis is characterized by swelling, tenderness, and elevated WBC count.

questions.questionText: A 23 year-old farmer presented to the OPD with abdominal pain and frequent vomiting of three hours duration. On examination, the abdomen is slightly distended with visible peristalsis. Plain abdominal X-ray showed a step ladder pattern air fluid level. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The step ladder pattern on X-ray suggests small bowel obstruction.

questions.questionText: A 17 year-old girl has noted cyclic stamp, lower abdominal pain that begins on the day of her menstrual flow and lasts for 2-3 days. Also, her menarche worsening in the last 2 years. Her periods are regular and pelvic examination is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Dysmenorrhea is characterized by painful menstruation.

questions.questionText: A hospital manager allocated a budget for three different activities. Which of the following is the next step in planning?
questions.explanation: Setting objectives is crucial after allocating a budget.

questions.questionText: A 31 year-old male presented came to the OPD after he sustained trauma to his right flank. He fell down from a two-story building. He complains of pain at the site and has gross hematuria. On examination, he is acutely sick looking in pain, BP=110/70mmhg, PR=96/min. There is a bruise over the right flank area that is tender to touch. Which organ is most likely injured?
questions.explanation: The kidney is commonly injured in flank trauma.

questions.questionText: A 35 year-old pregnant woman presents with fever, easily fatigability and change in mental status. On physical examination, BP=100/60mmhg, PR=108/min, RR=20/min, T=37.5°C and has pale conjunctiva and confused. Laboratory examination reveals hemoglobin=7g/dl, random blood sugar=30mg/dl and Plasmodium falciparum positive. Which of the following is the initial step in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: Glucose infusion is critical for managing hypoglycemia.

questions.questionText: An estimated 90 people out of 100 cases of Ebola died in the recent outbreak. What does this proportion represent?
questions.explanation: The case fatality rate indicates the proportion of deaths among diagnosed cases.

questions.questionText: A 20 year-old primigravida at 38 weeks was admitted in the second stage of labor and stayed for 90 minutes. Fetal heart beat is ranging between 80-90/min, vertex presentation with the occiput direct anterior, station +3 grade one molding. No cuput and grade-II meconium stained fluid. Which one of the following is the next best in management?
options: Expedite delivery by vacuum right away
Re-position her into the left lateral position
Secure IV line and await spontaneous vaginal delivery
questions.explanation: With fetal distress (heart rate 80-90/min and meconium staining) but favorable position (occiput anterior) and station (+3), vacuum-assisted delivery is the most appropriate choice to expedite delivery and minimize fetal hypoxia. Cesarean section would take longer and the fetal head is already deeply engaged.

questions.questionText: A 24 year-old GIII PI woman came with a complaint of decreased fetal movement at 33 weeks of gestation. What is the next best step in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: A biophysical profile is the best next step to assess fetal well-being.

questions.questionText: The recommended time to start folate supplementation for a mother who previously had a baby boy with myelomeningocele to prevent its recurrence in the next pregnancy is:
questions.explanation: Folate supplementation should start one month before conception to prevent neural tube defects.

questions.questionText: A 50 year-old male with chronic kidney disease presents with swelling of his feet. Physical examination revealed BP=150/90mmhg, PR=78/min, RR=18/min and bilateral ankle edema. Laboratory studies showed BUN=62 mg/dl, serum creatinine=3.2mg/dl, serum electrolytes (K⁺ level=5.6meq/l, Na⁺=146 meq/dl and total plasma cholesterol level of 260 mg/dl). Which of the following drugs improves the prognosis of his disease?
questions.explanation: ACE inhibitors like enalapril slow progression of chronic kidney disease by reducing intraglomerular pressure, decreasing proteinuria, and providing renoprotection. They're particularly beneficial in patients with hypertension and CKD, improving long-term outcomes and reducing mortality.

questions.questionText: A patient comes to your clinic with a complaint of hearing difficulty of one month duration. There is only a set of tuning forks for hearing assessment at the clinic. Which tuning fork should be used for the assessment?
questions.explanation: 512 Hz tuning fork is commonly used for hearing assessments.

questions.questionText: Which of the following clinical conditions that appear after pertussis vaccination is an absolute contraindication to subsequent administration of the vaccine?
questions.explanation: An immediate anaphylactic reaction is the only absolute contraindication to further doses of pertussis vaccine. Fever with convulsions, prolonged inconsolable crying, and shock-like states are considered precautions rather than absolute contraindications, requiring individual risk-benefit assessment.

questions.questionText: Sampling is the procedure some members of the given population are selected as representative part of the entire population. The information collected from the sample will be generalized to:
questions.explanation: The information collected from the sample is generalized to the target population.

questions.questionText: A 3 year-old boy is brought to the ER with high grade fever and shortness of breath of two days. On physical examination, RR=62/min, T=39°C, lower chest indrawing with bilateral basal coarse crepitations. The chest X-ray showed left basal lung pneumatocele. Which of the following is the most likely etiology?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is a common cause of lung abscesses in children.

questions.questionText: A 50 year-old woman presented with fever, cough and chest pain for two days. Chest X-ray showed pleural effusion. Pleural fluid analysis showed: WBC=5,000/mm³, with 90% neutrophils, pH=7.2, blood culture was positive for Streptococcus pneumonia. What is the next best in management of this patient besides antibiotics?
questions.explanation: Chest tube insertion is necessary for drainage of the pleural effusion.

questions.questionText: A 60 year old man is admitted with left side hemiparesis. CT reveals a middle cerebral artery infarct. What is the most significant risk factor for his condition?
questions.explanation: Hypertension is the most significant modifiable risk factor for stroke, increasing risk by 2-4 times. It directly damages blood vessels and accelerates atherosclerosis, making it more important than diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, or smoking in stroke development.

questions.questionText: A 55 year-old male comes to emergency OPD because of excruciating pain in his right big toe. He was diagnosed to have gouty arthritis. Which of the following is the best initial pharmacotherapy?
questions.explanation: Indomethacin or other NSAIDs are first-line treatments for acute gout attacks, reducing inflammation and pain. Allopurinol is used for long-term management to reduce uric acid levels but should not be started during an acute attack. Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic with no role in gout treatment, and morphine would only mask symptoms without addressing inflammation.

questions.questionText: A 22 year-old man is admitted to a burn unit after he sustained a scald burn. Three days after his admission, bright blood starts to ooze out through the NG-tube. He also has mild epigastric pain. Under GI endoscopy, multiple tiny ulcers in the corpus of the stomach are found. Which one of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Acute erosive gastritis can occur after burns due to stress.

questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions causes left lower quadrant abdominal pain?
questions.explanation: Diverticulitis typically presents with left lower quadrant pain.

questions.questionText: A 32 year-old man presented with an anterior neck mass of one year duration. On examination, he has a hoarse voice and a solitary 2cm x 2cm thyroid non-tender swelling on the right side which has firm consistency and is fixed to the underlying structures. There was no lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The fixed nature of the mass and hoarseness suggest thyroid cancer.

questions.questionText: A 26 year-old GII PI woman at 26 weeks of gestation came for ANC follow-up. She hasn't appreciated fetal movement yet. She had one episode of bleeding a month back and fetal heart beat was absent. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Missed abortion is characterized by the absence of fetal heart activity.

questions.questionText: A 4 day female neonate is brought to health center with failure to open her mouth and breast feed. She was well in the first three days after which the mother noticed excessive cry with stiff body posturing. The mother had no ANC follow-up and delivery was at home. What is the most likely diagnosis in this neonate?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are consistent with neonatal tetanus.

questions.questionText: A 65 year-old patient sustained a fall down accident three hours prior to presenting to the Emergency Room. He fell down with the arms extended. On examination, vital signs were normal with a right wrist deformity. X-ray showed displaced Colles' fracture. Which one is the best management option?
options: Skin traction for few days then casting
questions.explanation: For a displaced Colles' fracture, closed reduction to restore normal alignment followed by casting is the standard initial treatment. Simply applying a cast without reduction (option A) would result in healing with deformity, while open reduction (option C) is usually reserved for fractures that cannot be adequately reduced closed.

questions.questionText: A manager of a health center wants to provide BCG vaccine for infants on Fridays. Which of the following is the best management function that the manager used?
questions.explanation: Planning is essential for scheduling vaccination sessions.

questions.questionText: A 29 year-old man comes to emergency clinic with crampy abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea of one day. Stool microscopy shows trophozoites. Which one of the following is most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery characterized by bloody diarrhea.

questions.questionText: A 22 year-old nulliparous woman at 42+3 weeks gestation has a Bishop's score of 8. Which of the following would be the most appropriate induction method for this patient?
questions.explanation: With a favorable Bishop's score of 8 (indicating a ripe cervix), oxytocin is the most appropriate induction method. A Bishop's score of 10 would be unusually high for a nulliparous woman, so 8 is more realistic and still indicates a favorable cervix for induction.

questions.questionText: During a school survey on refraction, a 6 year-old girl was found to have a refractive error of (+3) on the left eye while the right eye was (+6). If the refractive error is not corrected by spectacles, which of the following is LEAST expected to happen?
questions.explanation: Floaters are not typically a consequence of uncorrected refractive errors.

questions.questionText: A 60 year-old alcoholic patient presented with fever, headache and neck pain of two days duration. On examination, body T=39°C and has neck stiffness. Bacterial meningitis was suspected but lumbar puncture was deferred because he has papilledema. Which one of the following is the best empiric therapy for this patient in addition to ampicillin?
questions.explanation: Ceftriaxone and vancomycin provide broad coverage for suspected bacterial meningitis.

questions.questionText: A 27 year-old woman complains of fever and fatigue. Non-tender, enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes are noted. Chest X-ray shows hilar lymphadenopathy and diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Lymph node biopsy shows non-caseating granuloma. Which drug is the most appropriate therapy?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation with non-caseating granulomas, hilar lymphadenopathy, and diffuse interstitial infiltrates is classic for sarcoidosis. Corticosteroids (glucocorticoids) are the first-line treatment for symptomatic sarcoidosis with significant organ involvement.

questions.questionText: A 66 year-old diabetic man suddenly collapsed in a hospital cafeteria and quick evaluation revealed an unresponsive man with no respiratory effort and pulseless carotids. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The lack of responsiveness, absent respiratory effort, and pulseless carotids definitively indicate cardiac arrest. Hypoglycemia would not cause absence of pulse or respiratory effort. Syncope involves temporary loss of consciousness with spontaneous recovery, and seizures typically involve muscle movements while maintaining pulse and respiration.

questions.questionText: A communal well water source development project was planned to be developed in a rural village. What needs to be identified for the outcome of the project to be effective?
options: Acceptance of the water source by the community
Cost of materials for development purpose
Electrolyte composition of the water source
Level of trace minerals in the water source
questions.explanation: Community acceptance and buy-in are critical for the success and sustainability of water projects. Without community involvement and acceptance, even technically sound water projects often fail due to lack of use, maintenance issues, or cultural incompatibility, regardless of the project's technical merits.

questions.questionText: A 60 year old man who had been smoking a pack of cigarettes daily for the last twenty years presented with one year history of increasing dyspnea on exertion and accumulation dry cough. Chest examination reveals hyper-resonance all over the lungs and decreased breath sounds. Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Emphysema is characterized by hyper-resonance and decreased breath sounds.

questions.questionText: A 47 year old man comes to the hospital complaining of epigastric pain that is exacerbated by eating. A test for Helicobacter pylori turned positive and endoscopy confirmed a duodenal ulcer. Which one is the most appropriate therapy?
questions.explanation: The triple therapy of amoxicillin, clarithromycin, and omeprazole is effective for H. pylori.

questions.questionText: A 20 year old woman who has been diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and started anti-tuberculosis treatment two weeks ago is found to be HIV positive on screening. On physical examination, she has pale conjunctiva and laboratory investigation shows CD4 count of 100 cells/μl. Which one of the following is most appropriate first antiretroviral regimen for this patient?
questions.explanation: TDF/3TC/EFV is the recommended regimen for HIV-TB co-infection because efavirenz has fewer interactions with rifampicin (TB medication) compared to nevirapine (NVP). Additionally, with severe immunosuppression (CD4 count 100 cells/μl), TDF is preferred over AZT due to the patient's anemia (pale conjunctiva).

questions.questionText: A 7 year old female patient who is on follow-up for bronchial asthma presented with shortness of breath of three hours. On physical examination she is conscious, able to talk in complete sentences, RR=62/min and PR=110/min. Chest examination reveals diffuse expiratory wheeze. What is the initial best step in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: Salbutamol is a bronchodilator and is the first-line treatment for acute asthma exacerbation.

questions.questionText: A 20 year-old man was seen at the emergency department following a road traffic accident of one hour duration. He has sustained trauma to the abdomen. On examination; vital signs: BP=80/50mmhg and PR=120/min. He has tire marks on the abdomen and it was tender. The patient is started on IV fluids. What is the next step in the management?
questions.explanation: Exploratory laparotomy is indicated in cases of suspected intra-abdominal injury with hemodynamic instability.

questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions causes left lower quadrant abdominal pain?
questions.explanation: Diverticulitis typically presents with left lower quadrant pain.

questions.questionText: A 32 year-old man presented with an anterior neck mass of one year duration. On examination he has a hoarse voice and a solitary 2cm x 2cm thyroid non-tender swelling on the right side which has firm consistency and is fixed to the underlying structures. There was no lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The fixed nature of the mass and hoarseness suggest thyroid cancer.

questions.questionText: A 26 year-old GII PI woman at 26 weeks of gestation came for ANC follow-up. She hasn't appreciated fetal movement yet. She had one episode of bleeding a month back and fetal heart beat was absent. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Missed abortion is characterized by the absence of fetal heart activity.

questions.questionText: A 4 day female neonate is brought to health center with failure to open her mouth and breast feed. She was well in the first three days after which the mother noticed excessive cry with stiff body posturing. The mother had no ANC follow-up and delivery was at home. What is the most likely diagnosis in this neonate?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are consistent with neonatal tetanus.

questions.questionText: A 65 year-old patient sustained a fall down accident three hours prior to presenting to the Emergency Room. He fell down with the arms extended. On examination, vital signs were normal with a right wrist deformity. X-ray showed displaced Colles' fracture. Which one is the best management option?
options: Skin traction for few days then casting
questions.explanation: Closed reduction and casting is the standard treatment for a Colles' fracture.

questions.questionText: A manager of a health center wants to provide BCG vaccine for infants on Fridays. Which of the following is the best management function that the manager used?
questions.explanation: Planning is essential for scheduling vaccination sessions.

questions.questionText: A 29 year-old man comes to emergency clinic with crampy abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea of one day. Stool microscopy shows trophozoites. Which one of the following is most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery characterized by bloody diarrhea.

questions.questionText: A 22 year-old nulliparous woman at 42+3 weeks gestation has a Bishop's score of 8. Which of the following would be the most appropriate induction method for this patient?
questions.explanation: With a favorable Bishop's score of 8 (indicating a ripe cervix), oxytocin is the most appropriate induction method. A Bishop's score of 10 would be unusually high for a nulliparous woman, so 8 is more realistic and still indicates a favorable cervix for induction.

questions.questionText: During a school survey on refraction, a 6 year-old girl was found to have a refractive error of (+3) on the left eye while the right eye was (+6). If the refractive error is not corrected by spectacles, which of the following is LEAST expected to happen?
questions.explanation: Floaters are not typically a consequence of uncorrected refractive errors.

questions.questionText: A 60 year-old alcoholic patient presented with fever, headache and neck pain of two days duration. On examination, body T=39°C and has neck stiffness. Bacterial meningitis was suspected but lumbar puncture was deferred because he has papilledema. Which one of the following is the best empiric therapy for this patient in addition to ampicillin?
questions.explanation: Ceftriaxone and vancomycin provide broad coverage for suspected bacterial meningitis.

questions.questionText: A 27 year-old woman complains of fever and fatigue. Non-tender, enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes are noted. Chest X-ray shows hilar lymphadenopathy and diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Lymph node biopsy shows non-caseating granuloma. Which drug is the most appropriate therapy?
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids are effective in treating sarcoidosis.

questions.questionText: A 66 year-old diabetic man suddenly collapsed in a hospital cafeteria and quick evaluation revealed an unresponsive man with no respiratory effort and pulseless carotids. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The absence of respiratory effort and pulselessness indicates cardiac arrest.

questions.questionText: A communal well water source development project was planned to be developed in a rural village. What needs to be identified for the outcome of the project to be effective?
options: Acceptance of the water source by the community
Cost of materials for development purpose
Electrolyte composition of the water source
Level of trace minerals in the water source
questions.explanation: Community acceptance is crucial for the success of water source projects.

questions.questionText: A 60 year old man who had been smoking a pack of cigarettes daily for the last twenty years presented with one year history of increasing dyspnea on exertion and accumulation dry cough. Chest examination reveals hyper-resonance all over the lungs and decreased breath sounds. Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Emphysema is characterized by hyper-resonance and decreased breath sounds.
